summary: Automatic model-fallback causes duplicated quota accounting and transient 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports spikes of 429 responses (quota exhausted) when their traffic triggers automatic fallback between primary and smaller model variants. The 429s appear for a subset of requests during normal traffic patterns and immediately after a model variant rollout.

Impact:
- Intermittent request failures for production search ranking calls (degraded UX for customers).
- Affects ~3% of requests during fallbacks; sustained for seconds to a few minutes.

Environment:
- Tenant: NimbleSearch Inc. (enterprise)
- Region: us-east-1
- Route config: primary pinned to redwood/gpt-medium-v2 with automatic fallback to redwood/gpt-small-v2 when latency or capacity constraints occur

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send steady stream of ranking requests (concurrency ~120) pinned to the primary route.
2) Force a minor model rollout on the primary (or simulate short degradation). The platform triggers automatic fallback to smaller variant for some requests.
3) Observe a burst of 429s in client logs during fallback window, not present when fallback disabled.

Observed behavior:
- Gateway logs show two quota increments for the same logical request in ~1% of cases: one for the original route and another for the fallback route. This leads to premature token exhaustion on tenant quota.

Expected behavior:
- A single logical request that triggers fallback should be accounted once against the tenant/route quota (with attribution to the effective serving model), not double-counted.

Relevant logs/snippets (customer provided):
- Request IDs: req-8f2c..., req-8f3a... timestamps matching fallback window
- Client error stream: 429 responses returned ~150ms after initial 202/stream-start for the same request id

Notes: This ticket differs from standard rate-limit spikes because it consistently correlates with fallback events rather than concurrency burst patterns.

I can reproduce double accounting in our quota-service metrics: two separate quota-assign increments within the same 200ms window for those request IDs when fallback occurs. Opening INT-2217 to track internal routing attribution change.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Eng (Priya Nair): Hypothesis: fallback currently executes as a separate routed request path after the initial route admits the request. The admission logic increments quota on admission and fallback logic doesn't reconcile or decrement the previous charge. Need to determine minimal change to ensure atomic accounting or to have the fallback produce a single combined accounting event.

2026-03-13 08:37 - Support (Jordan Blake): Customer confirmed that disabling automatic fallback removes the transient 429 pattern. We'll keep customer patched and coordinate a fix timeline with engineering.
investigation_notes: Checked gateway and quota-service metrics for timestamps provided; saw paired increments with identical tenant-id and proxied request hashes.
Reproduced in staging by forcing fallback: metrics show repeated quota.consume calls from routing layer (primary) followed by a fallback.consume call; no compensation executed.
Confirmed that the serving-runtime correctly served the fallback model, but quota attribution occurred twice across route and fallback layers.
Potential short-term mitigation: add idempotency key propagation from routing to quota-service so a subsequent fallback.consume can detect prior charge and skip or reconcile.

Long-term fix candidates: (A) Make fallback path perform quota transfer/transfer-replace instead of fresh consume; (B) Move quota accounting to an admission stage that finalizes after fallback decision.
Linked internal issue INT-2217 created to track design/PRs.
resolution:
Workaround provided: Support advised customer to temporarily disable automatic fallback on the affected route (done and confirmed by customer) which eliminated 429 bursts.

Planned fix: Engineering to implement idempotent quota operations for routed requests and update fallback to perform quota-replace semantics. Target patch in gateway v2.16.1 with rollout to staging 2026-03-18 and prod 2026-03-22 pending post-staging verification.

Follow-ups: update runbook to include fallback-related quota checks and add automated test to cover fallback accounting. Customer will be notified when fix is deployed and will be offered a follow-up validation session.
